title: New Algorithms for Incremental Minimum Spanning Trees and Temporal Graph Applications
summary: Processing graphs with temporal information (the temporal graphs) has become increasingly important in the real world. In this paper, we study efficient solutions to temporal graph applications using new algorithms for Incremental Minimum Spanning Trees (MST). The first contribution of this work is to formally discuss how a broad set of setting-problem combinations of temporal graph processing can be solved using incremental MST, along with their theoretical guarantees. Despite the importance of the problem, we observe a gap between theory and practice for efficient incremental MST algorithms. While many classic data structures, such as the link-cut tree, provide strong bounds for incremental MST, their performance is limited in practice. Meanwhile, existing practical solutions used in applications do not have any non-trivial theoretical guarantees. Our second and main contribution includes new algorithms for incremental MST that are efficient both in theory and in practice. Our new data structure, the AM-tree, achieves the same theoretical bound as the link-cut tree for temporal graph processing and shows strong performance in practice. In our experiments, the AM-tree has competitive or better performance than existing practical solutions due to theoretical guarantees, and can be significantly faster than the link-cut tree (7.8-11x in updates and 7.7-13.7x in queries).

title: A structure and asymptotic preserving scheme for the quasineutral limit of the Vlasov-Poisson system
summary: In this work, we propose a new numerical method for the Vlasov-Poisson system that is both asymptotically consistent and stable in the quasineutral regime, i.e. when the Debye length $λ$ is small compared to the characteristic spatial scale of the physical domain. Our approach consists in reformulating the Vlasov-Poisson system as a hyperbolic problem by applying a spectral expansion in the basis of Hermite functions in the velocity space and in designing a structure-preserving scheme for the time and spatial variables. Through this Hermite formulation, we establish a convergence result for the electric field toward its quasineutral limit together with explicit error estimates in $λ$. Following this path, we then propose a fully discrete numerical method for the Vlasov-Poisson system, inspired by the approach in arXiv:2306.14605, and rigorously prove that it is uniformly consistent in the quasineutral limit regime. Finally, we present several numerical simulations to illustrate the behavior of the proposed scheme. These results demonstrate the capability of our method to describe quasineutral plasmas, illustrate its stability and confirm its asymptotic preserving property.

title: ManiTaskGen: A Comprehensive Task Generator for Benchmarking and Improving Vision-Language Agents on Embodied Decision-Making
summary: Building embodied agents capable of accomplishing arbitrary tasks is a core objective towards achieving embodied artificial general intelligence (E-AGI). While recent work has advanced such general robot policies, their training and evaluation are often limited to tasks within specific scenes, involving restricted instructions and scenarios. Existing benchmarks also typically rely on manual annotation of limited tasks in a few scenes. We argue that exploring the full spectrum of feasible tasks within any given scene is crucial, as they provide both extensive benchmarks for evaluation and valuable resources for agent improvement. Towards this end, we introduce ManiTaskGen, a novel system that automatically generates comprehensive, diverse, feasible mobile manipulation tasks for any given scene. The generated tasks encompass both process-based, specific instructions (e.g., "move object from X to Y") and outcome-based, abstract instructions (e.g., "clear the table"). We apply ManiTaskGen to both simulated and real-world scenes, demonstrating the validity and diversity of the generated tasks. We then leverage these tasks to automatically construct benchmarks, evaluating high-level embodied decision-making through a grounded skill interface for agents built upon existing vision-language models (VLMs). Furthermore, we propose a simple yet effective method that utilizes ManiTaskGen tasks to enhance embodied decision-making. Overall, this work presents a cross-scene task generation framework facilitating both benchmarking and improvement of embodied decision-making agents. Our code is available at https://manitaskgen.github.io.

title: Equivariant Spherical Transformer for Efficient Molecular Modeling
summary: Equivariant Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) have significantly advanced the modeling of 3D molecular structure by leveraging group representations. However, message passing built only from exactly equivariant operations can have restricted practical expressiveness at a fixed representation degree. We introduce the Equivariant Spherical Transformer (EST), a plug-and-play module that applies Transformer attention to spherical spatial representations obtained from group representations. EST explicitly mixes information across sampled orientations, unlike prior orientation-wise spherical operations, while retaining a strong approximate equivariant inductive bias through near-uniform spherical sampling. As demonstrated by our experiments on challenging benchmarks like OC20, MPtrj and QM9, EST-based models achieve state-of-the-art performance. For the complex molecular systems within OC20, small models empowered by EST can outperform some larger models and those using additional data. We characterize the ideal closed-domain condition under which the continuous operation is exactly equivariant and empirically quantify the finite-sampling accuracy--equivariance--memory trade-off used in practice.

title: From Images to Signals: Are Large Vision Models Useful for Time Series Analysis?
comments: The manuscript has been withdrawn by the authors to undergo substantial revisions. A thoroughly revised version will be submitted in the future
summary: Transformer-based models have gained increasing attention in time series research, driving interest in Large Language Models (LLMs) and foundation models for time series analysis. As the field moves toward multi-modality, Large Vision Models (LVMs) are emerging as a promising direction. In the past, the effectiveness of Transformer and LLMs in time series has been debated. When it comes to LVMs, a similar question arises: are LVMs truely useful for time series analysis? To address it, we design and conduct the first principled study involving 4 LVMs, 8 imaging methods, 18 datasets and 26 baselines across both high-level (classification) and low-level (forecasting) tasks, with extensive ablation analysis. Our findings indicate LVMs are indeed useful for time series classification but face challenges in forecasting. Although effective, the contemporary best LVM forecasters are limited to specific types of LVMs and imaging methods, exhibit a bias toward forecasting periods, and have limited ability to utilize long look-back windows. We hope our findings could serve as a cornerstone for future research on LVM- and multimodal-based solutions to different time series tasks.

title: BNPO: Beta Normalization Policy Optimization
summary: Reinforcement learning with rule-based, binary-valued reward functions has been shown to significantly enhance the reasoning capabilities of large language models. These models typically rely on REINFORCE-based policy optimization methods, such as REINFORCE with baseline and group relative policy optimization (GRPO). However, a key limitation is that existing methods either ignore reward normalization or use static normalization schemes, which fail to adapt to the evolving policy during training. This mismatch can lead to unstable gradient estimates and hinder training stability. To address this issue, we propose Beta Normalization Policy Optimization (BNPO), a novel method that adaptively normalizes rewards using a Beta distribution with dynamically updated parameters. By aligning normalization with the changing policy distribution, BNPO enables more accurate, lower-variance gradient estimation and promotes stable training dynamics. We provide theoretical analysis showing that BNPO reduces variance and generalizes both REINFORCE and GRPO under binary-valued rewards. In addition, we introduce an advantage decomposition mechanism to extend BNPO to more complex reward settings. Experimental results demonstrate that BNPO achieves state-of-the-art performance among policy optimization methods on reasoning tasks.

title: Caterpillar GNN: Replacing Message Passing with Graph-Level Aggregation
summary: Message-passing graph neural networks (MPGNNs) dominate modern graph learning. Typical efforts enhance MPGNN's expressive power by enriching the adjacency-based aggregation. In contrast, we introduce a graph-level aggregation over walk incidence-based matrices that are constructed to deliberately trade off some expressivity for stronger and more structured inductive bias. This approach allows for gradual scaling between classical message-passing and simpler methods based on walks. Drawing on weighted automata, we ensure our gradual scaling is polynomial-time and avoids the combinatorial explosion of colored walks. Our second result characterizes the expressive power at each scale using homomorphism counts over a hierarchy of generalized caterpillar graphs. Based on these foundations, we propose Caterpillar GNNs that substantially reduce the number of nodes in the hidden layers of the computational graphs on real-world datasets. This gradual reduction does not obstruct learning, enabling a systematic study of lower-order expressivity. We further describe benchmark settings where task-aligned expressivity supports learning.

title: Subjective Experience in AI Systems: What Do AI Researchers and the Public Believe?
summary: Whether AI systems are perceived to have subjective experience has scientific, ethical, and governance implications. Yet little is known about how AI researchers and the public view this possibility. We surveyed 582 AI researchers who published in leading AI venues and 825 nationally representative US adults about the likelihood, identification, and governance of AI systems with subjective experience. We find that both AI researchers and the public think it is unlikely that AI systems have subjective experience now, but believe it is more likely than not they will by century's end. Both groups believe multidisciplinary expertise will be important in identifying AI subjective experience, support developers implementing safeguards now, and agree that, if created, subjectively experiencing AI systems should have moral responsibilities and be held accountable. Both groups also show substantial disagreement on many moral and policy questions. Our results underline the importance of building more detailed, evidence-based understanding of public and expert opinion on this contentious issue.

title: Infinite lexicographic products of positional objectives
summary: This paper contributes to the study of positional determinacy of infinite duration games played on potentially infinite graphs with neutral transitions. Recently, [Ohlmann, TheoretiCS 2023] established that positionality of prefix-independent objectives is preserved by finite lexicographic products. We propose two different notions of infinite lexicographic products indexed by arbitrary ordinals, and extend Ohlmann's result by proving that they also preserve positionality. In the context of one-player positionality, this extends positional determinacy results of [Grädel and Walukiewicz, Logical Methods in Computer Science 2006] to edge-labelled games and arbitrarily many priorities for both Max-Parity and Min-Parity. Moreover, we show that the Max-Parity objectives over countable ordinals are complete for the infinite levels of the difference hierarchy over $Σ^0_2$ and that Min-Parity is complete for the class $Σ^0_3$. We obtain therefore positional languages that are complete for all those levels, as well as new insights about closure under unions and neutral letters.

title: AblationBench: Evaluating Automated Planning of Ablations in Empirical AI Research
comments: Findings of the EMNLP 2026; Project page: https://ablation-bench.github.io/
summary: Language model agents are increasingly used to automate scientific research, yet evaluating their scientific contributions remains a challenge. A key mechanism to obtain such insights is through ablation experiments. To this end, we introduce AblationBench, a benchmark suite for evaluating agents on ablation planning tasks in empirical AI research. It includes two tasks: AuthorAblation, which helps authors propose ablation experiments based on a method section and contains 83 instances, and ReviewerAblation, which helps reviewers find missing ablations in a full paper and contains 350 instances. For both tasks, we develop LM-based judges that serve as an automatic evaluation framework. Our experiments with frontier LMs show that these tasks remain challenging, with the best-performing LM system identifying only 45% of the original ablations on average, below human-level performance. We observe an inverse performance trend between the author and reviewer tasks, which we attribute to differences in model grounding. Lastly, we analyze the limitations of current LMs on these tasks, and find that chain-of-thought prompting outperforms an agent-based approach. Our data is available on https://huggingface.co/collections/ai-coscientist/ablationbench, and our code is available on https://github.com/ai-scientist-bench/ablation-bench .

AI.title_translation: AblationBench：评估经验性AI研究中消融实验的自动化规划
AI.tldr: AblationBench是一个用于评估语言模型代理在AI研究中规划消融实验的基准套件，发现当前LMs表现不佳，远低于人类水平。
AI.motivation: 语言模型代理越来越多地用于自动化科学研究，但评估其科学贡献仍然是一个挑战。消融实验是获取此类见解的关键机制。因此，本文旨在引入一个基准套件来评估代理在经验性AI研究中消融规划任务上的能力。

AI.translation: 语言模型代理越来越多地用于自动化科学研究，然而评估它们的科学贡献仍然是一个挑战。获取此类洞察的关键机制是通过消融实验。为此，我们引入了AblationBench，这是一个用于评估代理在经验性AI研究中消融规划任务上的基准套件。它包括两个任务：AuthorAblation，帮助作者基于方法部分提出消融实验，包含83个实例；以及ReviewerAblation，帮助审稿人发现完整论文中缺失的消融实验，包含350个实例。对于这两个任务，我们开发了基于LM的评判器作为自动评估框架。我们对前沿LMs的实验表明，这些任务仍然具有挑战性，表现最佳的LM系统平均只能识别45%的原始消融实验，低于人类水平。我们观察到作者和审稿人任务之间存在反向性能趋势，我们将其归因于模型接地（model grounding）的差异。最后，我们分析了当前LMs在这些任务上的局限性，发现链式思考（chain-of-thought）提示优于基于代理的方法。我们的数据可在https://huggingface.co/collections/ai-coscientist/ablationbench获取，我们的代码可在https://github.com/ai-scientist-bench/ablation-bench获取。
AI.summary: 该论文介绍了AblationBench，一个用于评估语言模型代理在经验性AI研究中规划消融实验能力的基准套件。它包含AuthorAblation（作者提出消融实验）和ReviewerAblation（审稿人发现缺失消融实验）两个任务，并开发了基于LM的自动评估框架。实验结果表明，当前领先的语言模型在此类任务上表现不佳，远低于人类水平，且在不同任务间存在性能差异，链式思考提示表现优于基于代理的方法。研究强调了LMs在自动化科学研究中规划消融实验方面的局限性。

title: Isotonic Quantile Regression Averaging for uncertainty quantification of electricity price forecasts
summary: Quantifying the uncertainty of forecasting models is essential to assess and mitigate the risks associated with data-driven decisions, especially in volatile domains such as electricity markets. In this paper, we propose a computationally efficient isotonic variant of Quantile Regression Averaging (QRA), called Isotonic Quantile Regression Averaging (iQRA), for generating probabilistic forecasts from ensembles of point forecasts. Building on QRA, we introduce stochastic order constraints as a hyperparameter-free regularization mechanism that reduces computational complexity while maintaining competitive forecast accuracy. We further demonstrate that the same isotonic regularization principle can be applied to the smoothed estimator of QRA. In an extensive forecasting study of two European day-ahead electricity markets, we show that iQRA and its smoothed variant consistently rank among the top state-of-the-art postprocessing methods in terms of reliability and sharpness. It produces well-calibrated prediction intervals, with smoothed iQRA providing superior reliability even when compared against coverage-oriented conformal prediction. We further introduce a battery arbitrage evaluation, showing that the leading probabilistic methods achieve the highest profit per trade and that probabilistic risk control improves the economic value of trading decisions. Isotonic regularization offers a scalable hyperparameter-free variable selection for linear quantile regression, making iQRA attractive for practical decision-support systems in energy markets.

title: End-to-End On-Device Quantization-Aware Training for LLMs at Inference Cost
summary: Quantization reduces the deployment cost of large language models (LLMs). However, post-training quantization (PTQ) cannot fine-tune model parameters and often degrades accuracy in low-bit settings, while quantization-aware training (QAT) requires backpropagation and incurs high memory overhead. We propose ZeroQAT, a zeroth-order QAT framework supporting both weight and activation quantization. By using forward-only gradient estimation, ZeroQAT removes backpropagation and substantially reduces memory and computation while retaining end-to-end optimization benefits. We further introduce a lightweight variant of ZeroQAT for quantized fine-tuning, which freezes and pre-quantizes most parameters to further cut memory usage. Experiments show that ZeroQAT consistently outperforms representative PTQ and QAT baselines while requiring significantly less memory. For example, ZeroQAT enables fine-tuning of a 13B model at extremely low bit-widths (e.g., 2-4 bits) on a single 8GB GPU, and even allows fine-tuning a 6.7B model on a OnePlus 12 smartphone, demonstrating its practicality for end-to-end QAT on resource-limited edge devices.

title: L-MARS: Legal Multi-Agent System with Agentic Search and Citation-Faithfulness Audit
comments: 14 pages, 2 figures, 4 tables. Accepted at the AI for Law Workshop at ICML 2026 (PMLR 356)
summary: Large language models are increasingly deployed for legal question answering, where evaluations typically focus on multiple-choice accuracy. This measure overlooks a common failure: whether the citation source attached to an answer exists and supports the rule the system attributes to it. We present L-MARS, an open multi-agent legal QA system with agentic search and judge-driven evidence checks, and audit it claim by claim against its cited source. Each atomic claim is labelled with a six-class taxonomy and scored with strict-ALCE under cross-provider judging, where the answerer and verifier come from different model families. On a stratified 100-question Bar Exam audit, retrieval barely moves accuracy, yet the multi-turn judge loop lifts strict citation F1 from 0.13 (naive RAG) to 0.25 and cuts the no-citation rate from 34% to 13%. We further introduce Faith-Search, a post-draft step that re-verifies and repairs unreachable citations; it drops the unreachable rate below 1% but does not improve F1 over the multi-turn loop, so we report it as a targeted reachability intervention rather than a faithfulness breakthrough. A 50-question LegalSearchQA case study confirms the picture: retrieve-then-draft pipelines saturate near 0.75 citation F1, while a single-agent web-search baseline collapses to 0.22 under external audit.

title: Encoding of musical structures in hidden units of restricted Boltzmann machines
summary: Restricted Boltzmann machines (RBMs) are energy-based models originating from statistical physics. In this study, we investigate how musical structures are represented in the hidden layer of a Bernoulli-Bernoulli RBM trained on binary piano-roll representations of J.~S.~Bach's music. By examining the visible patterns induced by individual hidden units, we find that the hidden layer primarily captures local temporal and pitch-statistical features rather than explicit musical concepts such as melodies, chords, or keys. Free-energy comparisons show that the trained RBM assigns higher probabilities to the examined musical inputs than to digit or noise patterns. Analysis using t-SNE, cosine similarity, and PCA reveals that hidden representations are sensitive to absolute pitch and input overlap, with transposed versions of the same piece not necessarily mapped close together. Generated samples exhibit local pitch organization but limited long-range coherence. These findings illustrate how a simple statistical-physics model captures certain regularities in structured musical data while highlighting its limitations in representing higher-level musical relationships.

title: Sentinel Agents for Secure and Trustworthy Agentic AI in Multi-Agent Systems
comments: 23 pages, 11 figures. v2: the preliminary evaluation of v1 is replaced by a new evaluation on a balanced 1,000-message corpus with ablation, local LLM benchmark, aggregation and calibration analyses; paper restructured; references updated
summary: Multi-agent systems (MAS) built on large language models (LLMs) increasingly share a common conversational space, in which a single adversarial or erroneous message can propagate from one agent to many. This paper proposes Sentinel Agents, a dedicated security layer that monitors inter-agent communication with rule-based checks, behavioral analysis and LLM-based semantic inspection, and reports to a Coordinator Agent that enforces policy, for example by quarantining misbehaving agents. We describe the architecture, its deployment patterns and monitoring layers, and we evaluate a continuous-listener prototype on a balanced corpus of 1,000 synthetic messages (500 attacks across five families and 500 benign messages) with two local LLMs. LLM inspection with Gemma 4 12B reached F1 0.86 at a false-positive rate of 0.11, against 0.38 for rules alone. Combining components by logical OR did not improve on it, while a cascade in which only high-precision rules act on their own matched it. Calibrating the thresholds of the more conservative Qwen3 8B on a development split raised its held-out F1 from 0.56 to 0.80, and on multi-turn conversations the behavioral check detected patterns the rules missed but could not tell legitimate repetition from probing. The value of combining detectors therefore depends on the model, on its calibration and on the aggregation rule, and the results yield practical guidance for deploying Sentinel Agents.
